newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end stronger on tame inflation data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end stronger on tame inflation data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, pulled higher by gains in U.S. Treasuries, following the release of weaker-than-expected U.S. producer price data, analysts said.

"The general trend in the bond market was set in place by this morning's economic reports in the U.S. and Canada. In the U.S. we saw solid inflation numbers that said there's no concern about inflation right now," said John Johnston, deputy chief economist with Royal Bank of Canada.
Canada's 8.0 percent bond due 2023 rose C$0.15 to C$101.42 to yield 7.870 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 15/32 to yield 7.07 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 80 basis points from 78 points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian and U.S. bonds firmed this morning after the U.S. Labor Department said the monthly producer price index minus food and energy costs fell 0.1 percent. Economists had forecast an increase of 0.1 percent.
The Labor Department also reported initial jobless claims of 338,000 in the week ended September 7. Economists had expected claims would total 329,000.
In Canada, Statistics Canada reported new motor vehicle sales fell 2.9 percent seasonally adjusted in July from June.
Investors are now looking ahead to the release of Canadian and U.S. consumer price data tomorrow, dealers said.

In auction news, the Government of Canada said it plans to auction on September 18 a total of C$2.4 billion of bonds with an unspecified coupon maturing June, 2007. The Bank of Canada said it will acquire at least C$240 million of the issue.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.18 to C$97.15 to yield 7.401 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 11/32 to yield 6.87 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 53 basis points from 49 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.78 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.27 percent.
